name: Simons and Beating Peaks
description: My loveliest wishes dissolved into the air; At eighteen, I poured my dreams into the mic to share. — SHUN, 720 We call an array $$$b$$$ of length $$$m$$$ cool if and only if: There exists no index $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \lt i \lt m$$$) such that $$$b_i=\max(\{b_{i-1}, b_i, b_{i+1}\})$$$. Simons has an array $$$a$$$ of size $$$n$$$. Initially, the array is a permutation$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$. He must perform the following operation until the array is cool : Choose an index $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \lt i \lt n$$$) such that $$$a_i=\max(\{a_{i-1}, a_i, a_{i+1}\})$$$. Then, he can remove either $$$a_{i-1}$$$ or $$$a_{i+1}$$$ from the array. After removal, a gap appears in the array, and the left and right sides of the gap will be rejoined. Find the minimum number of operations for Simons to perform. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A permutation of length $$$n$$$ is an array consisting of $$$n$$$ distinct integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ in arbitrary order. For example, $$$[2,3,1,5,4]$$$ is a permutation, but $$$[1,2,2]$$$ is not a permutation ($$$2$$$ appears twice in the array), and $$$[1,3,4]$$$ is also not a permutation ($$$n=3$$$ but there is $$$4$$$ in the array).
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 5\cdot 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$3\le n\le 5\cdot 10^5$$$) — the size of $$$a$$$. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ ($$$1\le a_i\le n$$$, all $$$a_i$$$-s are distinct) — the array Simons has initially. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5\cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print a single integer — the minimum number of operations for Simons to perform.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2205D — Simons and Beating Peaks [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
